newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Ansett launches ticketless travel.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Ansett launches ticketless travel.

text.p: Ansett Australia said on Tuesday it would become the first Australian airline to introduce ticketless travel to its domestic network.
The carrier said its ticketless travel innovation, called 'E-Ticket', would be available from January 1, 1997 to customers who booked domestic travel directly with the airline.

"Ansett's E-Ticket system is based on United Airlines /Air Canada technology which was introduced to Ansett's reservations environment with some minor enhancements for the Australian market," the airline said in a statement.
Under the ticketless system customers followed the normal booking procedure but instead of being issued with a ticket could check in by presenting photo identification, Ansett said.
Ansett's general manager sales and marketing, Rick Ellis, said the airline was striding ahead with plans which would give retail travel agents access to the E-Ticket by mid-1997.
Ellis said Ansett had approached major computerised reservation systems (CRS) firms to fast-track the development of automated links between their systems and Ansett's.

"We've already had very successful preliminary talks with Sabre and Galileo, which between them distributed Ansett product to about 90 percent of the airline's agents, regarding interfacing to our system and we'll be meeting with them again this month to further advance technical implementation plans," Ellis said.

Ansett said E-Ticket would not be available for bookings on its international services, nor on services it code-shared with other carriers. Ansett is 50 percent owned by News Corp Ltd and 50 percent by Air New Zealand Ltd.
